analysis.title: FedEx Corp. (FDX): 3Q Ahead on International; Some Quarterly Noise and Costs to Lap, But Still Comfortable with LT Path
key_insights: GS reiterates Buy on FDX with a 12-month price target of $390 (unchanged), 28.0% above the $304.58 price. The target is 17.5x P/E on Q5-Q8 EPS of $22.50. The stock trades at 14.8x GS's calendar 2027 EPS forecast.

3Q26 adjusted EPS of $3.74 (text) or $3.75 (Exhibit 10) was well ahead of the $3.18 and $3.31 cited in the text. The beat came mainly from International, where margin and EBIT were well ahead of forecast. International EBIT was $297M against a GS estimate of $144.8M and consensus of $190.8M.

Management raised the CY26 EPS guide to $18.00-$18.60 from $16.90-$18.10, with revenue growth of about 12% (from 11%) and EBIT of $5.9B (from $5.8B). The new midpoint of $18.30 compares with GSe $17.85 and Visible Alpha $17.80 going into the quarter.

US Domestic is the soft spot. 3Q Domestic margin was 6.6% against a GS estimate of 7.1%, down 20bp YoY, and management expects it to be down somewhat again in 4Q. GS attributes the miss to higher purchased transportation (PT) cost and fuel headwinds of about 30bp, both expected to continue into 4Q.

Purchased transportation was $6,455M against a GS estimate of $5,808.3M (+11%). GS ties this to driver tightness in third-party trucking, which it says other transports also reported this quarter. Third-party PT around trucking is 10-12% of transportation miles, with company drivers and service providers at 70% and rail at 15%.

Management cited two levers to offset elevated PT cost into 4Q and 2027: insourcing and raising rates to cover the cost. GS expects Domestic margin to improve YoY on a full-year 2027 basis and sees the cost headwind lapping more completely in 2H27. GS flags investor concern about the timing of the inflection and the need to see cost mitigation come through.

The CY26 EBIT bridge runs from $5.0B in CY25 to about $5.9B. Volume net of cost adds $800M (from $600M), yields add $3.7B (unchanged) and Freight stranded cost reduction adds $100M. Headwinds are $2.7B of base expense increases (from $2.6B), $800M of variable incentive compensation and $200M from the new pilot contract starting in July.

US Domestic volume grew 2% YoY in 3Q, in line with GS's 2.1%. Yield grew 7%, in line with GS's 7.3%. Ground Commercial volume rose 3.5% on the high-value B2B push, while Home Delivery/Economy volume grew only 1% and is expected to stay negative as FDX improves revenue quality mix.

International Express volume fell 4% YoY, weaker than GS's -2.5%, but yield grew 17%, in line with GS's 16.9%. International Export Package volume grew +8%/+7%/+9% in Jul/Aug/Sep. International freight was up 15% in pounds and 29% in gross revenue.

GS expects margin gains in International from premium parcel mix, higher-yielding export volumes and European station consolidation, similar to what FDX did in the US. The longer-term International margin target is 8% in 2029.

GS estimate changes, per the report's EPS table (the text labels the same figures one year later): CY26E rises to $18.38 from $17.85 on the higher 3Q and better 4Q outlook. CY27E falls to $20.60 from $21.00 on lower Domestic margins at the start of the year from higher PT. CY28E is nearly unchanged at $23.50 from $23.55, and the 2029 EPS estimate is unchanged at $25.80.

The Buy case rests on commercial and cost initiatives (higher-yield B2B, selective B2C, cost transformation, AI integration), capital discipline, EPS potential approaching $25 by CY2029, possible freight demand recovery with operating leverage, and reasonable valuation.

GS says quarterly noise was expected as FDX moves from a fiscal to a calendar year basis after the LTL spin. It also says calendar-year estimates cannot be modeled accurately until restated financial statements are released.

market_movers.rationale: Reiterates Buy and the $390 target after an International-led 3Q beat and a raised CY26 guide. GS trims CY27E EPS to $20.60 on slower Domestic margins from higher purchased transportation cost, but leaves the 2029 EPS estimate of $25.80 unchanged.

earnings_insights: FDX 3Q26 adjusted (recurring) EPS reported at $3.75 in GS Exhibit 10, or $3.74 in the Bottom Line text. The text cites GS/Visible Alpha consensus of $3.18 and $3.31. Exhibit 10 shows a GS estimate of $3.18 and Exhibit 11 shows consensus of $3.33. Reported (GAAP) EPS was $1.21 on reported net income of $290M versus $896M recurring.

3Q26 revenue was reported at $22,855M against a GS estimate of $22,430.7M and consensus of $22,591.7M. Operating income was $1,197M against a GS estimate of $1,059.4M and consensus of $1,114.4M. Operating margin was 5.2% against consensus of 4.9%.

3Q26 segment EBIT as reported. International was $297M (4.0% margin in Exhibit 10, 3.9% in the text) against a GS estimate of $144.8M and consensus of $190.8M. US Domestic was $972M (6.6% margin) against a GS estimate of $1,040.6M (7.1%) and consensus of $1,006.8M (6.8%).

3Q26 cost lines as reported versus GS estimates. Purchased transportation was $6,455M against $5,808.3M (+11%). Fuel was $1,270M against $1,160.5M (+9%). Salaries and employee benefits were $7,434M against $7,739.6M (-4%).

Management raised the CY26 guide on 10/29 (company guidance, a forecast). EPS is $18.00-$18.60 ($18.30 midpoint) from $16.90-$18.10 ($17.50 midpoint), revenue growth is about 12% (from 11%) to about $92.4B, EBIT is about $5.9B (from $5.8B), and the tax rate is 22.5%. The midpoint implies EPS growth of 23.4% off CY25 EPS of $14.83.

Domestic margin was down 20bp YoY in 3Q and management expects it to be down again somewhat in 4Q on fuel and elevated purchased transportation cost. GS expects YoY Domestic margin improvement on a full-year 2027 basis.

CY26 YTD (1Q-3Q summed) recurring EPS was $11.98 reported versus a GS estimate of $11.00 and consensus of $11.22. Earlier quarters in the same exhibits: 1Q26 recurring EPS of $3.25 versus consensus of $3.61 and a GS estimate of $3.73, and 2Q26 recurring EPS of $4.98 versus consensus of $4.28 and a GS estimate of $4.09.

GS CY estimates per its EPS table (diluted, pre-exceptionals): CY26E $18.38 (old $17.85), CY27E $20.60 (old $21.00), CY28E $23.50 (old $23.55). GS revenue estimates rise to $92,350.6M for CY26E (from $91,093.9M), $96,221.8M for CY27E and $100,397.8M for CY28E. The text calls the first three figures 2027, 2028 and 2028 EPS, which looks like a one-year label shift. The 2029 EPS estimate is $25.80, unchanged.

trade_ideas.description: Buy FDX, 12-month price target $390 (17.5x P/E on Q5-Q8 EPS of $22.50), 28.0% upside from $304.58
trade_ideas.rationale: International margin is ahead of plan, pricing power supports about 12% revenue growth, and GS sees the 3-year earnings path intact despite near-term Domestic cost pressure.
trade_ideas.risk: Inability to attract labor, inability to get core pricing upgrades, an industrial or e-commerce slowdown, and failure to execute cost savings through DRIVE and Network 2.0.

risk_factors: Near term: elevated third-party purchased transportation cost and fuel headwinds are expected to keep Domestic margin down YoY in 4Q26 and into early 2027.
Additional 2026 headwinds: $800M of variable incentive compensation and $200M from the new pilot contract starting in July.
Inability to attract labor, causing ongoing network inefficiencies and making the margin forecast harder to achieve.
Inability to get core pricing upgrades, which would limit margin recovery given inflationary pressures.
A slowdown in the industrial or e-commerce economy, impacts to global trade from issues with overseas partners, rising inflation, tariffs or higher interest rates.
Inability to execute cost savings through the DRIVE and Network 2.0 initiatives.
Any attempt by labor to challenge the generally non-union nature of FedEx operations.
Inability to model calendar-year estimates accurately until restated financial statements are released.

tension_points.bull_case: International margin of 3.9% is well ahead of plan, with the 8% target for 2029 intact. FDX has two levers (insourcing and raising rates) to offset elevated purchased transportation cost. GS expects YoY Domestic margin improvement on a full-year 2027 basis, with the cost headwind lapping more completely in 2H27. Volume growth and core price discipline should let both Domestic and International margin potential materialize over the next three years.
tension_points.bear_case: Domestic margin was down 20bp YoY in 3Q and is expected down again somewhat in 4Q. Fuel and elevated purchased transportation costs persist, driver tightness in third-party trucking is industry-wide, and incentive compensation ($800M) and the new pilot contract ($200M) add to 2026 costs. GS flags possible investor concern about the timing of the inflection and the need to see cost mitigation come to fruition.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Domestic margin failing to improve YoY on a full-year 2027 basis, with purchased transportation cost not lapping by 2H27 and the insourcing and rate-increase levers not showing up in results.

theme_stances.key_argument: International earnings strength from premium parcel and higher-yielding export volumes, plus European station consolidation, should deliver meaningful margin improvement over the next several years.
theme_stances.evidence: earnings strength in International from leaning into premium parcel

theme_stances.key_argument: Driver tightness in third-party purchased transportation is raising FDX US Domestic costs, likely weighing on 4Q26 margin and into 2027 before mitigation takes hold.
theme_stances.evidence: driver tightness in 3rd party PT is causing higher than expected costs
